summary: IANA created the OTN Signal Type subregistry under the GMPLS Signaling Parameters registry in RFC 7139. This standards-track RFC changes its allocation policy to allow registration through Specification Required.

eli5.summary: Changing the rules for adding new entries to a list, so more values can be added with a written spec.

subtitle: IANA may now register new OTN signal types under Specification Required, not only Standards Action.

tldr.problem: The OTN Signal Type subregistry allowed only the Standards Action policy, so every new value needed a Standards Track RFC.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7892 updates RFC 7139 so the subregistry uses Standards Action for Standards Track documents and Specification Required for other documents.
tldr.outcome: New OTN signal types can be registered from a written specification that is not a Standards Track RFC.

facts.label: New policy
facts.value: Standards Action for Standards Track, Specification Required for others

today: RFC 7892 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 7139. No later RFC is recorded as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: The Registry and Its Old Policy
sections.content:
IANA maintains the OTN Signal Type subregistry of the Generalized Multi-Protocol Label Switching (GMPLS) Signaling Parameters registry. It holds OTN signal types as defined in RFC 4328 and updated by RFC 7139.

The subregistry was defined to use only the Standards Action registration policy from RFC 5226.
sections.eli5: There is an official list of signal types, and it only accepted new entries through the strictest process.

sections.title: The Policy Change
sections.content:
RFC 7892 updates RFC 7139 so that the subregistry may also use the Specification Required policy from RFC 5226.

IANA has set the registration policies to Standards Action for Standards Track documents and Specification Required for other documents.
sections.eli5: Big official papers still use the strict door. Other well-written papers can now use a second door.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The document introduces no new security considerations for the existing GMPLS signaling protocols. It points to RFC 7139 for specific security measures and to RFC 5920 for an overview of vulnerabilities and protections in the GMPLS control plane.
sections.eli5: Changing who may add to the list does not open any new risk, so the note points to the existing safety guides.
